own_solution.law: Bead on rotating hoop (rotating frame): equilibrium cos(theta) = g/(omega^2 R); small-oscillation angular frequency Omega = omega sin(theta); period T = 2 pi/Omega
assumptions: omega^2 R > g so off-axis equilibrium exists (19.6 > 9.8)
platform at rest (inertial) unless stated otherwise

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T9510 and T9186 say 'a few metres per second squared' instead of 2.1 m/s^2; acceptable only as numeral-free controls.

notes: Base: cos(theta) = 9.8/(49*0.4) = 0.5, theta = 60 deg, Omega = 7 sin60 = 6.0622 rad/s, T = 1.0365 s. With upward platform acceleration 2.1 m/s^2, g_eff = 11.9: cos(theta) = 0.60714, sin^2 = 0.63138, Omega^2 = 30.9375, Omega = 5.5621, T = 1.1296 s (equilibrium still exists, 11.9 < 19.6). Mass cancels from both equilibrium and oscillation equations (C). Crane load has no coupling to the hoop (D). Earlier-run acceleration leaves no state (D).
